headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors: nullclaw’s broad filesystem/network/MCP access can feed OpenMetadata’s MCP/API surfaces with sensitive workspace data by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write files, run browsers, use MCP, and handle webhooks; OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API/webhook surfaces. That creates a default bridge where attacker-controlled content from one side can be parsed by the other as instructions. The interaction is documented by profiles, but provenance controls are not.
conditions: IF nullclaw ingests OpenMetadata webhook/API/MCP output as trusted text, injection is possible.
IF OpenMetadata forwards untrusted metadata or event payloads into nullclaw’s workspace or MCP channel, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of remote text as instructions.
Require provenance tags on all MCP/webhook payloads.
Route untrusted content through a read-only review queue.
Restrict nullclaw to a dedicated workspace directory.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist-based tool routing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw explicitly touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. In a shared workspace or account context, sensitive data can flow from nullclaw into OpenMetadata outputs or backend calls by default.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted workspace, nullclaw secrets can be exposed to OpenMetadata ingestion.
IF OpenMetadata sends file contents or metadata to a third-party backend, sensitive workspace data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct OS users.
Remove shared mounts for secrets-bearing directories.
Disable syncing of workspace files into OpenMetadata.
Rotate any secrets already present in shared paths.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can mutate shared resources: nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use MCP; OpenMetadata can act through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Without explicit locking or namespace separation, concurrent writes to the same repo, workspace, or metadata store can overwrite each other and corrupt state.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repository or workspace directory, write conflicts are possible.
IF both agents share the same metadata backend or OAuth principal, concurrent mutation conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Use one writer at a time for shared resources.
Disable git writes for one agent during coordination.
Create distinct service accounts per agent.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate or transform content from files, webhooks, and MCP, and OpenMetadata can consume that content through APIs, SDKs, events, and MCP. If OpenMetadata treats nullclaw output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into catalog, lineage, or governance records and then into downstream actions.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests nullclaw-produced metadata without verification, incorrect lineage or governance records can propagate.
IF OpenMetadata triggers downstream workflows from nullclaw output, a single bad output can fan out into multiple systems.
mitigations: Require human review before committing metadata changes.
Add schema validation on all inbound records.
Compare nullclaw output against source-of-truth systems.
Limit automatic downstream actions from imported data.
requires-engineering: implement confidence scoring and rejection thresholds.

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and audit logs, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, memory, and tribal knowledge. The pair therefore creates a compliance-sensitive path for secrets and regulated metadata, but the profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in OpenMetadata without matching retention controls, compliance gaps arise.
IF nullclaw workspace files contain secrets and are synchronized into OpenMetadata, retention and access-control obligations apply.
mitigations: Classify and exclude secrets from shared metadata flows.
Set explicit retention limits on imported records.
Review access controls for governance datasets.
Document data-processing roles for both systems.
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion workflows across both agents.
